title: The Last Thorn Anew
premise: Dominic Whitlock, a memory-thief and ledger-keeper for the Vellum Guild, discovers their own name and tonight's date inscribed in a century-old book of prophecies. When the prophecy's magic drags them into a conspiracy to resurrect the Thorn King — an ancient sovereign whose return would reignite a war that froze the world once before — Dominic must ally with the very people they've been robbing: a disgraced knight, a child who remembers futures, and the guildmaster who betrayed them. The secret Dominic carries, stolen from the guild's deepest vault, is proof that the Thorn King never died but sleeps beneath the city, sustained by memories the guild has been feeding him for generations. In the end, Dominic chooses justice outside the law: they give the sleeping king back every stolen memory at once, letting him finally die, and the found family they've gathered rebuilds the guild into something that gives rather than takes.
about_author: C. M. Delacroix is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging rare books in a flooded cathedral library before turning to fiction. They write about thieves, ledgers, and the terrible arithmetic of survival from a drafty attic full of unlabeled keys.

chapters.title: The Ledger Opens Both Ways
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. On an ordinary night of inventorying impossible trades — bottled grief, a decade of someone's childhood — Dominic finds tonight's date written in a century-old prophetic ledger, followed by their own name. The emotional beat is cold dread: a keeper of records realizing the record was kept first.

chapters.title: What the Vault Keeps Warm
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Investigating the vault's restricted shelf, Dominic steals a sealed memory meant for delivery to an unnamed client and glimpses a sleeping figure crowned in thorns beneath the city. Beat: awe curdling into guilt as they realize the guild's prosperity has a heartbeat.

chapters.title: The Knight Who Owes Nothing
chapters.summary: Ser Aldric's POV. A disgraced knight hired by the guild to escort a 'delivery' recognizes the seal on Dominic's stolen memory as his dead order's own. He confronts Dominic instead of reporting them. Beat: two liars recognizing each other's wounds and striking a wary bargain.

chapters.title: A Child Made of Tomorrows
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren, an eight-year-old the guild keeps for her prophetic flashes, dreams of thorns blooming through snow and tells Dominic she's dreamed them before — always right before someone dies. Beat: tenderness and terror entwined; Dominic decides to protect her rather than use her.

chapters.title: The Guildmaster's Smile
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Guildmaster Corvane summons Dominic, reveals he knows the memory is missing, and offers partnership instead of punishment — because he wants the Thorn King awake. Beat: betrayal sharpened by charm; Dominic realizes the prophecy named them because Corvane needs a thief.

chapters.title: Running on Stolen Feet
chapters.summary: Ser Aldric's POV. Dominic, Aldric, and Wren flee the guildhouse through the undercity while Corvane's collectors hunt them using memories of Dominic's own face. Beat: desperate momentum and the first fragile laughter among the three — the found family taking shape mid-flight.

chapters.title: The Price of One More Night
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Hiding in a hospice, Wren uses her gift to buy the group safe passage, paying with a year of her own future memories. Dominic rages; Wren insists survival is worth its price. Beat: the theme made flesh — what we spend to keep each other.

chapters.title: Where the Old War Sleeps
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. In the ruins of Aldric's order's chapterhouse, they find murals confirming the Thorn King's history: he ended the last long winter by taking every painful memory in the realm — and never gave them back. Beat: moral vertigo; the monster was once a mercy.

chapters.title: Ledgers of the Damned
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Decoding the prophetic ledger fully, Dominic learns the guild has fed the sleeping king curated memories for a hundred years to keep him dreaming peacefully — and Corvane plans to feed him a war. Beat: understanding hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Collector's Kindness
chapters.summary: New character Maren's POV. A guild collector catches Wren alone but, holding one of Dominic's stolen memories of her own lost daughter, lets them go. Beat: compassion inside the machine; even hunters are being hunted by what they carry.

chapters.title: Snow Begins to Fall
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The first unnatural snow of the new long winter falls out of season as Corvane begins waking the king with war-memories. The city panics; old hatreds resurface. Beat: the stakes become weather — time itself now an enemy.

chapters.title: What We Buried in Each Other
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. Cornered, Aldric confesses he helped bury the truth of the Thorn King a generation ago and let his order be destroyed to keep it silent. Dominic refuses to condemn him. Beat: forgiveness as an act of defiance against the law that ruined them both.

chapters.title: The Market of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. To fund their way into the vaults, the trio sells small mercies at the black market — returned memories to grieving strangers. Beat: warmth amid winter; the group discovers what a guild could be if it gave instead of took.

chapters.title: Corvane's Open Hand
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Corvane captures Wren and offers a trade: the stolen memory for the girl, plus a seat beside him when the king wakes. He genuinely believes a strong king will end suffering. Beat: temptation with a human face; Dominic almost believes it too.

chapters.title: Thieves' Justice
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren, moved by what she carried, brings evidence of Corvane's plan to the trio instead of the guild. Together they plan a heist no law would sanction: steal the king's death. Beat: alliance across enemy lines; justice assembled outside every court.

chapters.title: Down Where the Roots Remember
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The descent into the root-vaults beneath the city, past centuries of stored memories humming like a hive. Beat: claustrophobic wonder; Dominic feels every stolen life pressing at their edges.

chapters.title: The Long Winter's Heart
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. They reach the Thorn King — vast, thorn-crowned, half-awake, already tasting Corvane's war-dreams. Aldric kneels to his old sovereign and asks pardon. Beat: reverence and horror; the climax's stage is set.

chapters.title: Everything We Carried
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV (climax). Corvane arrives; Wren, freed by Maren, breaks the dream-feed. Dominic pours every stolen memory back into the king at once — all the grief, love, and guilt of a century. The king weeps, thanks them, and dies at last. Corvane, unmade by the truth flooding the vault, collapses. Beat: sacrifice as release, not loss.

chapters.title: After the Thaw
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The false winter breaks. The city wakes to a guildhouse emptied of its vaults, its stores of memories returned anonymously overnight. Beat: quiet astonishment; the world is lighter and doesn't know why.

chapters.title: The New Ledger
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The survivors refound the guild as something honest: brokers of returned memories, healers of grief, answerable to no crown. Dominic writes the first entry of a new ledger. Beat: purpose rebuilt from ruin.

chapters.title: What Wren Chose to Keep
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Offered restoration of everything she spent, Wren declines most of it, keeping only her memories of the journey. Beat: bittersweet agency; the price of survival paid willingly is not a wound but a choice.

chapters.title: The Last Thorn, Uprooted
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV (coda). On the anniversary night that once bore their name in prophecy, Dominic burns the old ledger page and plants a rose where the root-vaults stood. Found family around a small fire. Beat: peace earned, not granted — the story closes on warmth against any winter.
